claim: Recent discoveries have identified extreme cellular diversity in the brain.
source: Recent discoveries of extreme cellular diversity in the brain warrant rapid development of technologies to access specific cell populations within heterogeneous tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a motivation for the work.

claim: Available approaches for engineering-targeted technologies for new neuron subtypes are low yield.
source: Available approaches for engineering-targeted technologies for new neuron subtypes are low yield, involving intensive transgenic strain or virus screening.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background context.

claim: SNAIL is an improved virus-based strategy for cell labeling and nuclear isolation from heterogeneous tissue.
source: Here, we present Specific Nuclear-Anchored Independent Labeling (SNAIL), an improved virus-based strategy for cell labeling and nuclear isolation from heterogeneous tissue.
evidence: This is the main claim about the technology presented in the paper.

claim: SNAIL works by leveraging machine learning and computational approaches to identify DNA sequence features that confer cell type-specific gene activation.
source: SNAIL works by leveraging machine learning and other computational approaches to identify DNA sequence features that confer cell type-specific gene activation and then make a probe that drives an affinity purification-compatible reporter gene.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of SNAIL as presented in the abstract.

claim: Two novel SNAIL probes that target parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) neurons were designed and validated.
source: As a proof of concept, we designed and validated two novel SNAIL probes that target parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key result.

claim: Nuclear isolation using SNAIL in wild-type mice is sufficient to capture characteristic open chromatin features of PV+ neurons in the cortex, striatum, and external globus pallidus.
source: Nuclear isolation using SNAIL in wild-type mice is sufficient to capture characteristic open chromatin features of PV+ neurons in the cortex, striatum, and external globus pallidus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key finding.

claim: Expression from a mouse PV+ SNAIL enhancer sequence was enriched in PV+ neurons of the macaque cortex.
source: The SNAIL framework also has high utility for multispecies cell probe engineering; expression from a mouse PV+ SNAIL enhancer sequence was enriched in PV+ neurons of the macaque cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as evidence for cross-species utility.

claim: Single-cell sequencing has identified over a hundred molecularly distinct neuronal populations in the mammalian cortex.
source: Contemporary advancements in single-cell sequencing have identified over a hundred molecularly distinct neuronal populations in the mammalian cortex (Lake et al., 2016; Saunders et al., 2018; Tasic et al., 2018; Hodge et al., 2019; Zeisel et al., 2015), including several small subpopulations of gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic neurons with specialized functions that are critical for the control of neuronal inhibition (Kepecs and Fishell, 2014; Lim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: GABAergic neurons include several small subpopulations with specialized functions critical for the control of neuronal inhibition.
source: Contemporary advancements in single-cell sequencing have identified over a hundred molecularly distinct neuronal populations in the mammalian cortex (Lake et al., 2016; Saunders et al., 2018; Tasic et al., 2018; Hodge et al., 2019; Zeisel et al., 2015), including several small subpopulations of gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic neurons with specialized functions that are critical for the control of neuronal inhibition (Kepecs and Fishell, 2014; Lim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Transgenic mouse strains targeting major inhibitory neuron subclasses are widely used today.
source: Transgenic mouse strains targeting major inhibitory neuron subclasses, including parvalbumin-expressing (PV+), somatostatin-expressing (SST+), and serotonergic (5-HT+) neurons, are widely used today and have been instrumental toward our understanding of these cell types (Madisen et al., 2010; Taniguchi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: AAV-PHP.B and AAV-PHP.eB are AAV variants that cross the blood–brain barrier to transduce the central nervous system.
source: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) technologies became particularly attractive with the invention of AAV variants that cross the blood–brain barrier to transduce the central nervous system, AAV-PHP.B, and AAV-PHP.eB (Chan et al., 2017; Deverman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Enhancer activity can be extremely selective, even more so than the activity of most genes and their associated promoters.
source: Enhancer activity can be extremely selective, even more so than the activity of most genes and their associated promoters (Hoffman et al., 2013; Kellis et al., 2014; Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium et al., 2015 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: ATAC-seq is an advantageous technique for defining potential cell type-specific enhancer regions because of its high nucleotide resolution and compatibility with small cell populations.
source: ATAC-seq (Buenrostro et al., 2013) is an advantageous technique for defining potential cell type-specific enhancer regions because of its high nucleotide resolution and its compatibility with small cell populations and even with single-cell technologies (Buenrostro et al., 2015b; Cusanovich et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Chromatin accessibility is a noisy approximation for enhancer activity.
source: Though convenient, chromatin accessibility is a noisy approximation for enhancer activity and differentially accessible sequence elements often fail to produce selective expression in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field.

claim: Differentially accessible sequence elements often fail to produce selective expression in vivo.
source: Though convenient, chromatin accessibility is a noisy approximation for enhancer activity and differentially accessible sequence elements often fail to produce selective expression in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field.

claim: Machine learning models could be applied as additional in silico filters to reduce the burden of experimental screening in cell type-specific AAV development.
source: We hypothesized that machine learning models could be applied as additional in silico filters to reduce the burden of experimental screening in cell type-specific AAV development while maintaining the convenience of ATAC-seq as the sole input data requirement.
evidence: This is the hypothesis of the study.

claim: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and support vector machines (SVMs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance on predicting enhancer activity from sequence.
source: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) (Le Cun et al., 1989) and support vector machines (SVMs), for example, have achieved state-of-the-art performance on predicting enhancer activity from sequence (Arvey et al., 2012; Ghandi et al., 2014; Zhou and Troyanskaya, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: SNAIL probes have the unique advantage of an affinity purification-compatible fluorescent reporter that can be used to isolate rare cell types.
source: Similar to our previously described Cre-activated AAV technology cSNAIL (Lawler et al., 2020), SNAIL probes have the unique advantage of an affinity purification-compatible fluorescent reporter that can be used to isolate rare cell types (Mo et al., 2015; Deal and Henikoff, 2010; Lawler et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: SNAIL probes are stand-alone AAVs driven by cell type-specific enhancer sequences selected through machine learning models.
source: Unlike cSNAIL, which relies on Cre activation, SNAIL probes are stand-alone AAVs driven by cell type-specific enhancer sequences selected through machine learning models.
evidence: This describes the key difference between SNAIL and cSNAIL.

claim: SNAIL probes may be used in a wide variety of systems, including wild-type mice, primates, and other species.
source: Thus, SNAIL probes may be used in a wide variety of systems, including wild-type mice, primates, and other species.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of SNAIL.

claim: In the mouse primary motor cortex, PV+ SNAIL probes labeled PV+ neurons with >70% specificity when compared to Pvalb antibody staining.
source: In the mouse primary motor cortex, PV+ SNAIL probes labeled PV+ neurons with >70% specificity when compared to Pvalb antibody staining.
evidence: This is a key experimental result from the study.

claim: PV+ SNAIL probes in the mouse primary motor cortex were more specific to GABAergic PV+ neurons than the common Pvalb-2A-Cre/Ai14 mouse strain.
source: PV+ SNAIL probes in this context were more specific to GABAergic PV+ neurons than the common Pvalb-2A-Cre/Ai14 mouse strain.
evidence: This is a key experimental result from the study.

claim: Isolated populations of tagged cells from the cortex, striatum, and external globus pallidus were each heavily enriched for known PV+ open chromatin signatures.
source: In addition, isolated populations of tagged cells from the cortex, striatum, and external globus pallidus (GPe) were each heavily enriched for known PV+ open chromatin signatures.
evidence: This is a key experimental result from the study.

claim: Nucleotide-resolution model interpretation highlighted a collection of 14 TF binding motif families contributing to PV+ neuron-specific enhancer activation.
source: Nucleotide-resolution model interpretation highlighted a collection of 14 TF binding motif families contributing to PV+ neuron-specific enhancer activation.
evidence: This is a key result from the computational analysis.

claim: At least one SNAIL probe showed PV+ neuron selectivity in both mouse and macaque.
source: Machine learning can aid in cross-species probe design as well; at least one SNAIL probe showed PV+ neuron selectivity in both mouse and macaque.
evidence: This is a key experimental result from the study.

claim: SVMs were built to discriminate sequences of differential OCRs between two cell populations.
source: We built machine learning classifiers, primarily SVMs, to discriminate sequences of differential OCRs between two cell populations.
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: The similarity between sequences is determined based on gapped k-mer count vectors.
source: The similarity between sequences is determined based on gapped k-mer count vectors, that is, the number of occurrences of all short subsequences of length k, tolerating some gaps or mismatches, as implemented by LS-GKM (Ghandi et al., 2014; Lee, 2016).
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study, supported by citations.

claim: Training sequences were required to have a minimum fold difference in chromatin accessibility between the two cell types used to define the classes.
source: We imposed upfront that training sequences have a minimum fold difference in chromatin accessibility between the two cell types used to define the classes.
evidence: This describes a methodological choice in the study.

claim: A neuron vs. astrocyte classifier achieved an auROC of 0.95 and an auPRC of 0.98.
source: Both models performed well on held-out data, achieving auROCs of 0.95 and 0.93 and auPRCs of 0.98 and 0.82 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: An excitatory neuron vs. inhibitory neuron classifier achieved an auROC of 0.93 and an auPRC of 0.82.
source: Both models performed well on held-out data, achieving auROCs of 0.95 and 0.93 and auPRCs of 0.98 and 0.82 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The Gfap promoter sequence was classified as astrocyte-specific in the neuron vs. astrocyte model.
source: The Gfap promoter sequence, which has a heavy astrocyte bias in vivo, was classified as astrocyte-specific in our neuron vs. astrocyte model (5580 astrocyte-specific enhancers evaluated; Gfap ranks 3298/5580).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: The Camk2a promoter sequence was scored as neuron-specific in the neuron vs. astrocyte model.
source: The same neuron vs. astrocyte model scored the Camk2a promoter and Dlx promoter sequences, which are known to have neuron-specific activity, as neuron-specific (14,347 neuron-specific enhancers evaluated; Camk2a = rank 13,300/14,347, Dlx = rank 9736/14,347).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: The Dlx promoter sequence was scored as neuron-specific in the neuron vs. astrocyte model.
source: The same neuron vs. astrocyte model scored the Camk2a promoter and Dlx promoter sequences, which are known to have neuron-specific activity, as neuron-specific (14,347 neuron-specific enhancers evaluated; Camk2a = rank 13,300/14,347, Dlx = rank 9736/14,347).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: The excitatory vs. inhibitory neuron model predicted the Camk2a sequence to have an excitatory neuron preference.
source: Also consistent with empirical expectations, the excitatory vs. inhibitory neuron model predicted the Camk2a sequence to have an excitatory neuron preference and the Dlx sequence to have an inhibitory neuron preference (15,391 excitatory neuron-specific enhancers evaluated; Camk2a = rank 11,541; 4,608 inhibitory neuron-specific enhancers tested; Dlx = rank 1142/4608) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The excitatory vs. inhibitory neuron model predicted the Dlx sequence to have an inhibitory neuron preference.
source: Also consistent with empirical expectations, the excitatory vs. inhibitory neuron model predicted the Camk2a sequence to have an excitatory neuron preference and the Dlx sequence to have an inhibitory neuron preference (15,391 excitatory neuron-specific enhancers evaluated; Camk2a = rank 11,541; 4,608 inhibitory neuron-specific enhancers tested; Dlx = rank 1142/4608) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Binary classifiers were trained on sequences underlying differential ATAC-seq peaks between PV+ neurons and another population.
source: Again, we trained binary classifiers on sequences underlying differential ATAC-seq peaks between two cell populations (PV+ neurons and another population).
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: Multiple models were built comparing PV+ neurons to either PV- cells generally, excitatory neurons, VIP+ neurons, or SST+ neurons.
source: To maximize sequence signal detection, we built several models comparing PV+ neurons to either PV- cells generally, excitatory neurons, VIP+ neurons, or SST+ neurons.
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: Input data sources varied to be either 'population-derived' or 'sn-derived'.
source: In addition, we varied the input data source to be either 'population-derived' (from bulk ATAC-seq sequencing on purified nuclei populations) or 'sn-derived' (from single-nucleus open chromatin assays such as droplet-based snATAC-seq).
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: Multiple modeling strategies were implemented, including linear gapped k-mer SVMs, nonlinear gapped k-mer SVMs using the radial basis function (rbf), and CNNs.
source: Finally, we implemented multiple modeling strategies, including linear gapped k-mer SVMs, nonlinear gapped k-mer SVMs using the radial basis function (rbf), and CNNs.
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: ATAC-seq was conducted on PV+ and PV- nuclei of Pvalb-2A-Cre mice using cSNAIL technology.
source: First, to define potential PV+ neuron and PV- cell enhancer sequences in the mouse cortex in a population data-driven manner, we conducted ATAC-seq on the PV+ and PV- nuclei of Pvalb-2A-Cre mice. We isolated the nuclei populations using previously described Cre-dependent AAV affinity purification technology, cSNAIL (Lawler et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: Population-derived PV+ vs. PV- SVMs could predict the correct classification on held-out data with test set auROC = 0.87–0.88 and auPRC = 0.95–0.96.
source: Population-derived PV+ vs. PV- SVMs could predict the correct classification on held-out data with high accuracy (test set auROC = 0.87–0.88, auPRC = 0.95–0.96; gray lines Figure 1b and c), indicating that there were substantial sequence pattern differences between the PV+ and PV- classes and that the models were able to learn these differences.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: There were substantial sequence pattern differences between the PV+ and PV- classes.
source: Population-derived PV+ vs. PV- SVMs could predict the correct classification on held-out data with high accuracy (test set auROC = 0.87–0.88, auPRC = 0.95–0.96; gray lines Figure 1b and c), indicating that there were substantial sequence pattern differences between the PV+ and PV- classes and that the models were able to learn these differences.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational results.

claim: Population-derived SVMs directly discriminating between enhancer sequences of PV+ neurons and other neuron subtypes performed well (auROC = 0.89–0.93, auPRC = 0.79–0.92).
source: These models performed well (auROC = 0.89–0.93, auPRC = 0.79–0.92; Figure 1b and c), demonstrating that, even at the level of neuron subtypes, OCR sequence information is rich enough to reliably distinguish cell type-specific activity.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Even at the level of neuron subtypes, OCR sequence information is rich enough to reliably distinguish cell type-specific activity.
source: These models performed well (auROC = 0.89–0.93, auPRC = 0.79–0.92; Figure 1b and c), demonstrating that, even at the level of neuron subtypes, OCR sequence information is rich enough to reliably distinguish cell type-specific activity.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational results.

claim: CNNs are better equipped to learn higher-order interactions between sequence features due to CNNs' capacity for flexible feature representation and automated feature selection.
source: Compared with SVMs, CNNs are better equipped to learn higher-order interactions between sequence features due to CNNs' capacity for flexible feature representation and automated feature selection (Le Cun et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The CNNs were highly accurate (auROC = 0.95–0.96, auPRC = 0.76–0.97).
source: The CNNs were highly accurate (auROC = 0.95–0.96, auPRC = 0.76–0.97; Figure 1d).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Single-nucleus sequencing technologies can be applied to measure neuron subtype-resolution open chromatin without cell sorting.
source: Single-nucleus sequencing technologies can be applied to measure neuron subtype-resolution open chromatin without cell sorting by performing several parallel microreactions that introduce unique cell barcodes into ATAC-seq sequencing reads and then clustering the cells with similar chromatin profiles.
evidence: This describes a known technology in the field.

claim: Five pairwise linear gapped k-mer SVMs were trained to discriminate differential open chromatin sequences from snATAC-seq clusters.
source: We trained five pairwise linear gapped k-mer SVMs to discriminate differential open chromatin sequences from snATAC-seq clusters or groups of clusters.
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: Single-nucleus-derived SVMs were able to classify cell type-specific enhancer sequences with high accuracy (auROC = 0.89–0.93, auPRC = 0.72–0.92).
source: Single-nucleus-derived SVMs were also able to classify cell type-specific enhancer sequences with high accuracy (auROC = 0.89–0.93, auPRC = 0.72–0.92; Figure 1e).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Models built independently from different data sources identified similar sequence contributions for equivalent tasks.
source: Moreover, models built independently from different data sources identified similar sequence contributions for equivalent tasks.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: When scoring the population-derived sequences through both the population-derived SVMs and the single-nucleus-derived SVMs, individual sequences had highly similar scores.
source: When scoring the population-derived sequences through both the population-derived SVMs and the single-nucleus-derived SVMs, individual sequences had highly similar scores (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Model predictions were evaluated on 34 externally validated successful and unsuccessful PV+ probe enhancer candidates from Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020.
source: To ensure that the neuron subtype-level models were identifying signatures that were relevant for the specific purpose of creating selective PV+ neuron viruses, we evaluated model predictions on 34 externally validated successful and unsuccessful PV+ probe enhancer candidates from Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020, named E1–E34.
evidence: This describes the validation approach used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: The enhancer sequence from the probe with the lowest PV+ specificity (E4; 14% specificity) received a negative score from every model.
source: Importantly, the enhancer sequence from the probe with the lowest PV+ specificity (E4; 14% specificity) received a negative score from every model, and two of the enhancer sequences with highest cortical PV+ specificity (E22 and E29; 94% specificity) received high positive scores from every model (Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: Two of the enhancer sequences with highest cortical PV+ specificity (E22 and E29; 94% specificity) received high positive scores from every model.
source: Importantly, the enhancer sequence from the probe with the lowest PV+ specificity (E4; 14% specificity) received a negative score from every model, and two of the enhancer sequences with highest cortical PV+ specificity (E22 and E29; 94% specificity) received high positive scores from every model (Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: On the complete set of enhancers, SVM score was predictive of the PV+ specificity group (p=0.008).
source: On the complete set of enhancers, SVM score was predictive of the PV+ specificity group (p=0.008), and differential activity log2 fold difference had a weak association with PV+ specificity group (p=0.069) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5c).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Differential activity log2 fold difference had a weak association with PV+ specificity group (p=0.069).
source: On the complete set of enhancers, SVM score was predictive of the PV+ specificity group (p=0.008), and differential activity log2 fold difference had a weak association with PV+ specificity group (p=0.069) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5c).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Within the subset of enhancers with high log2 fold difference (log2 fold difference > 1), the log2 fold difference was not associated with specificity group (p=0.601).
source: Within the subset of enhancers with high log2 fold difference (log2 fold difference > 1), the log2 fold difference was not associated with specificity group (p=0.601), while SVM score was weakly associated (p=0.057) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5d).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Within the subset of enhancers with high log2 fold difference (log2 fold difference > 1), SVM score was weakly associated with specificity group (p=0.057).
source: Within the subset of enhancers with high log2 fold difference (log2 fold difference > 1), the log2 fold difference was not associated with specificity group (p=0.601), while SVM score was weakly associated (p=0.057) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5d).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Unlike log2 fold difference scores alone, SVM scores may limit false-positive candidates and improve efficient enhancer AAV selection.
source: Unlike log2 fold difference scores alone, SVM scores may limit false-positive candidates and improve efficient enhancer AAV selection.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational results.

claim: Sequence E29 was predicted to have PV+ neuron-specific activity due to a central Mef2 motif site and nearby Esrrg motif site, among others.
source: Sequence E29, within the Inpp5j locus, was predicted to have PV+ neuron-specific activity due to a central Mef2 motif site and nearby Esrrg motif site, among others (Figure 1—figure supplement 6, Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Sequence E22 was predicted to have PV+ specificity in part due to Nkx28 and Lhx6 motif sites.
source: Sequence E22, within the Tmem132c locus, was predicted to have PV+ specificity in part due to Nkx28 and Lhx6 motif sites (Figure 1—figure supplement 6, Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: SC1 was the highest predicted sequence candidate among true PV+ neuron-specific enhancer sequences.
source: Among true PV+ neuron-specific enhancer sequences that (i) were differential OCRs in PV+ vs. PV-, PV+ vs. EXC, and PV+ vs. VIP+ sorted population data and (ii) scored PV+ positive across all SVM evaluations (1755 sequences), SC1 was the highest predicted sequence candidate, while SC2 was in the 90th percentile (Figure 2b, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: SC2 was in the 90th percentile among true PV+ neuron-specific enhancer sequences.
source: Among true PV+ neuron-specific enhancer sequences that (i) were differential OCRs in PV+ vs. PV-, PV+ vs. EXC, and PV+ vs. VIP+ sorted population data and (ii) scored PV+ positive across all SVM evaluations (1755 sequences), SC1 was the highest predicted sequence candidate, while SC2 was in the 90th percentile (Figure 2b, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: SC1 and SC2 sequences were cloned into separate vectors upstream of the cSNAIL reporter gene, Sun1GFP.
source: SC1 and SC2 sequences were cloned into separate vectors upstream of the cSNAIL reporter gene, Sun1GFP.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: PV+ SNAIL probes directly rely on transcriptional activation from SC1 or SC2, without a minimal promoter.
source: To minimize off-target effects, PV+ SNAIL probes directly rely on transcriptional activation from SC1 or SC2, without a minimal promoter (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: When packaged with AAV-PHP.eB and delivered to the mouse through systemic injection, the SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP constructs promoted cortical fluorescence that was restricted to PV+ neurons.
source: When packaged with AAV-PHP.eB and delivered to the mouse through systemic injection, the SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP constructs promoted cortical fluorescence that was restricted to PV+ neurons, while the Ef1a virus did not (Figure 2c–e, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation, with reference to figures.

claim: The Ef1a virus did not promote cortical fluorescence restricted to PV+ neurons.
source: When packaged with AAV-PHP.eB and delivered to the mouse through systemic injection, the SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP constructs promoted cortical fluorescence that was restricted to PV+ neurons, while the Ef1a virus did not (Figure 2c–e, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation, with reference to figures.

claim: SC1 and SC2-mediated expression of Sun1GFP was restricted to Pvalb+ neurons in ~70–74% of cases.
source: Compared with immunohistochemistry-labeled Pvalb protein, SC1 and SC2-mediated expression of Sun1GFP was restricted to Pvalb+ neurons in ~70–74% of cases.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation.

claim: SC1 and SC2 SNAIL probes showed an 11-fold enrichment in precision over the Ef1a promoter.
source: This was an 11-fold enrichment in precision over the Ef1a promoter and notably an almost twofold enrichment over Cre reporter labeling in Pvalb-2A-Cre/Ai14 double transgenic mice (Figure 2c–e, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation, with reference to figures.

claim: SC1 and SC2 SNAIL probes showed an almost twofold enrichment over Cre reporter labeling in Pvalb-2A-Cre/Ai14 double transgenic mice.
source: This was an 11-fold enrichment in precision over the Ef1a promoter and notably an almost twofold enrichment over Cre reporter labeling in Pvalb-2A-Cre/Ai14 double transgenic mice (Figure 2c–e, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation, with reference to figures.

claim: Sun1GFP expression from SC1 and SC2 SNAIL probes labeled ~71–73% of Pvalb+ neurons.
source: On average, Sun1GFP expression from SC1 and SC2 SNAIL probes labeled ~71–73% of Pvalb+ neurons.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation.

claim: The rate of labeling is limited by the transduction properties of the AAV-PHP.eB capsid, which is expected to transduce 55–70% of neurons in the cortex.
source: The rate is limited by the transduction properties of the AAV-PHP.eB capsid, which is expected to transduce 55–70% of neurons in the cortex (Chan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Nuclei were isolated from Sun1GFP-expressing cells induced by SC1-Sun1GFP, SC2-Sun1GFP, or Ef1a-Sun1GFP SNAIL virus from the mouse cortex and ATAC-seq was performed.
source: Taking advantage of this property, we isolated Sun1GFP-expressing nuclei induced by SC1-Sun1GFP, SC2-Sun1GFP, or Ef1a-Sun1GFP SNAIL virus from the mouse cortex and performed ATAC-seq.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Both SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP cells were highly enriched for PV+ neurons.
source: Through comparison with known PV+ neuron ATAC-seq (via cSNAIL in the Pvalb-2A-Cre strain) and PV- or bulk ATAC-seq, including cSNAIL PV- cell fractions and Ef1a virus signatures, we determined that both SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP cells were highly enriched for PV+ neurons.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation.

claim: The first principal component, accounting for 84% of the total variance, separated known PV+ neuron samples from PV- and bulk tissue samples.
source: The first principal component, accounting for 84% of the total variance, separated known PV+ neuron samples from PV- and bulk tissue samples.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP samples grouped with the PV+ samples while Ef1a-Sun1GFP samples grouped with the PV- and bulk sample signatures.
source: Likewise, SC1-Sun1GFP and SC2-Sun1GFP samples grouped with the PV+ samples while Ef1a-Sun1GFP samples grouped with the PV- and bulk sample signatures (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, with reference to a figure.

claim: At the Pvalb locus, there were highly reproducible OCR signals between PV+ cSNAIL, PV+ snATAC-seq, SC1-Sun1GFP, and SC2-Sun1GFP samples that did not appear in bulk tissue, PV-, or Ef1a-Sun1GFP samples.
source: At the Pvalb locus, there were highly reproducible OCR signals between PV+ cSNAIL, PV+ snATAC-seq, SC1-Sun1GFP, and SC2-Sun1GFP samples that did not appear in bulk tissue, PV-, or Ef1a-Sun1GFP samples (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, with reference to a figure.

claim: Two different batches of cortical PV+ cSNAIL samples had a Pearson correlation of 0.86 and a Spearman correlation of 0.85.
source: To establish an upper limit for correlation, we compared two different batches of cortical PV+ cSNAIL samples, which had a Pearson correlation of 0.86 and a Spearman correlation of 0.85.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: The nonspecific Ef1a control virus had a Pearson correlation of 0.38 and a Spearman correlation of 0.26 with PV+ cSNAIL.
source: As a lower limit, we evaluated the nonspecific Ef1a control virus, which had a Pearson correlation of 0.38 and a Spearman correlation of 0.26.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: SC1 had a Pearson correlation of 0.85 and Spearman correlation of 0.84 with cSNAIL.
source: Within this range, SC1 and SC2 had very high correlation with cSNAIL, with SC1 achieving almost equivalent correlation as the two cSNAIL batches (SC1 Pearson = 0.85 and Spearman = 0.84; SC2 Pearson = 0.81 and Spearman = 0.79) (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, with reference to a figure.

claim: SC2 had a Pearson correlation of 0.81 and Spearman correlation of 0.79 with cSNAIL.
source: Within this range, SC1 and SC2 had very high correlation with cSNAIL, with SC1 achieving almost equivalent correlation as the two cSNAIL batches (SC1 Pearson = 0.85 and Spearman = 0.84; SC2 Pearson = 0.81 and Spearman = 0.79) (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, with reference to a figure.

claim: cSNAIL-isolated PV+ OCRs, SC1-isolated OCRs, and SC2-isolated OCRs were each significantly enriched for PV+ cluster-specific markers (34–47% overlap, hypergeometric p=0).
source: We found that cSNAIL-isolated PV+ OCRs, SC1-isolated OCRs, and SC2-isolated OCRs were each significantly enriched for PV+ cluster-specific markers (34–47% overlap, hypergeometric p=0), while OCRs from Ef1a-isolated cells were not enriched for PV+ cluster-specific markers (4% overlap, p=1).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: OCRs from Ef1a-isolated cells were not enriched for PV+ cluster-specific markers (4% overlap, p=1).
source: We found that cSNAIL-isolated PV+ OCRs, SC1-isolated OCRs, and SC2-isolated OCRs were each significantly enriched for PV+ cluster-specific markers (34–47% overlap, hypergeometric p=0), while OCRs from Ef1a-isolated cells were not enriched for PV+ cluster-specific markers (4% overlap, p=1).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: Ef1a OCRs had the highest enrichment for markers of a layer 4 excitatory neuron cluster (25% overlap, p=5.3 × 10–5).
source: Ef1a OCRs instead had the highest enrichment for markers of a layer 4 excitatory neuron cluster (25% overlap, p=5.3 × 10–5).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: cSNAIL PV+ ATAC-seq had an additional 8% overlap with excitatory cluster L5 PT markers (p=2.5 × 10–45).
source: We also note that cSNAIL PV+ ATAC-seq had an additional 8% overlap with excitatory cluster L5 PT markers (p=2.5 × 10–45), possibly reflective of Pvalb-2A-Cre line labeling in layer 5 parvalbumin-expressing excitatory neurons (Tanahira et al., 2009; Jinno and Kosaka, 2004; Roccaro-Waldmeyer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, supported by citations.

claim: SC1 and SC2 had no enrichment for cluster-specific OCRs of any cluster other than PV+ (≤2% overlap, p>0.1).
source: In fact, SC1 and SC2 had no enrichment for cluster-specific OCRs of any cluster other than PV+ (≤2% overlap, p>0.1), including the closely related SST+ neuron population.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: SC1 and SC2 SNAIL probes target a stricter subset of the cells than the Pvalb-2A-Cre mouse strain, likely restricted to PV+ inhibitory interneurons.
source: This suggests that SC1 and SC2 SNAIL probes target a stricter subset of the cells than the Pvalb-2A-Cre mouse strain, likely restricted to PV+inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: Many PV+ neurons throughout the brain have a common developmental origin in the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE).
source: Many PV+ neurons throughout the brain have a common developmental origin in the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE), but there are substantial OCR differences between mature PV+ neuron populations in different brain regions.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: There are substantial OCR differences between mature PV+ neuron populations in different brain regions.
source: Many PV+ neurons throughout the brain have a common developmental origin in the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE), but there are substantial OCR differences between mature PV+ neuron populations in different brain regions.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: Thousands of OCRs with differential accessibility between the cortex, striatum, and GPe were characterized (padj<0.01, |log2FoldDifference| > 1).
source: From cSNAIL-isolated PV+ populations in Pvalb-2A-Cre mice (Lawler et al., 2020), we characterized thousands of OCRs with differential accessibility between the cortex, striatum, and GPe (padj<0.01, |log2FoldDifference| > 1) (Figure 4a, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, with reference to figures.

claim: OCRs that were more accessible in cortical PV+ neurons relative to striatal and GPe PV+ had enrichment for Mef2 family motifs.
source: For example, OCRs that were more accessible in cortical PV+ neurons relative to striatal and GPe PV+ had enrichment for Mef2 family motifs, which are important in neuroplasticity (Donato et al., 2015), may play a role in specifying or maintaining the MGE PV+ neuron lineage in mouse and human (Mayer et al., 2018), and have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders involving the prefrontal cortex (Mitchell et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, supported by citations.

claim: Mef2 family motifs are important in neuroplasticity.
source: For example, OCRs that were more accessible in cortical PV+ neurons relative to striatal and GPe PV+ had enrichment for Mef2 family motifs, which are important in neuroplasticity (Donato et al., 2015), may play a role in specifying or maintaining the MGE PV+ neuron lineage in mouse and human (Mayer et al., 2018), and have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders involving the prefrontal cortex (Mitchell et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Mef2 family motifs may play a role in specifying or maintaining the MGE PV+ neuron lineage in mouse and human.
source: For example, OCRs that were more accessible in cortical PV+ neurons relative to striatal and GPe PV+ had enrichment for Mef2 family motifs, which are important in neuroplasticity (Donato et al., 2015), may play a role in specifying or maintaining the MGE PV+ neuron lineage in mouse and human (Mayer et al., 2018), and have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders involving the prefrontal cortex (Mitchell et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Mef2 family motifs have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders involving the prefrontal cortex.
source: For example, OCRs that were more accessible in cortical PV+ neurons relative to striatal and GPe PV+ had enrichment for Mef2 family motifs, which are important in neuroplasticity (Donato et al., 2015), may play a role in specifying or maintaining the MGE PV+ neuron lineage in mouse and human (Mayer et al., 2018), and have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders involving the prefrontal cortex (Mitchell et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: TFs with motifs enriched in PV+ neuron OCRs that are more open in striatum relative to cortex and GPe included Tgif1.
source: TFs with motifs enriched in PV+ neuron OCRs that are more open in striatum relative to cortex and GPe included Tgif1, a key homeodomain gene involved in holoprosencephaly (Taniguchi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data, supported by a citation.

claim: Tgif1 is a key homeodomain gene involved in holoprosencephaly.
source: TFs with motifs enriched in PV+ neuron OCRs that are more open in striatum relative to cortex and GPe included Tgif1, a key homeodomain gene involved in holoprosencephaly (Taniguchi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: At 6654 differential OCRs, GPe-specific PV+ OCRs were the most unique.
source: At 6654 differential OCRs, GPe-specific PV+ OCRs were the most unique and had TF motif enrichments, including the Lhx3, Pou5f1, Esrrg, and Pax3 motifs.

claim: GPe-specific PV+ OCRs had TF motif enrichments, including the Lhx3, Pou5f1, Esrrg, and Pax3 motifs.
source: At 6654 differential OCRs, GPe-specific PV+ OCRs were the most unique and had TF motif enrichments, including the Lhx3, Pou5f1, Esrrg, and Pax3 motifs.

claim: Enhancer scores were well correlated between the cortex and striatum models (Pearson = 0.73, Spearman = 0.72).
source: Enhancer scores were well correlated between the cortex and striatum models (Pearson = 0.73, Spearman = 0.72), indicating shared regulatory sequence determinants between PV+ neurons in the cortex and striatum.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: There was a low correlation between enhancer scores of the cortex and GPe models (Pearson = 0.25, Spearman = 0.24).
source: There was a low correlation between enhancer scores of the cortex and GPe models (Pearson = 0.25, Spearman = 0.24), indicating differences in the learned PV+ regulatory sequence properties in these regions.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: SC1 and SC2 sequences were predicted to have PV+-specific activation in both the striatum and GPe.
source: SC1 and SC2 sequences were predicted to have PV+-specific activation in both the striatum and GPe (Figure 4c and f).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Pearson correlation coefficients were similar or slightly lower for SC1 and SC2 in the striatum and GPe than for equivalent comparisons in the cortex.
source: Pearson correlation coefficients were similar or slightly lower for SC1 and SC2 in the striatum and GPe than for equivalent comparisons in the cortex, indicating less conservation between cSNAIL and SNAIL probe targets (SC1 cortex = 0.85, striatum = 0.71, GPe = 0.68; SC2 cortex = 0.81, striatum = 0.82, GPe = 0.73).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: SC1 and SC2 correlations with cSNAIL in striatum and GPe were substantially increased over Ef1a correlation with cSNAIL in these tissues.
source: Still, these were substantially increased over Ef1a correlation with cSNAIL in these tissues, especially for the striatum (Ef1a cortex = 0.38, striatum = 0.18, GPe = 0.51).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: SC1 and SC2 SNAIL viruses seem to generalize to the striatum and GPe, though they may not be as robust as they are within the cortical context.
source: From these interpretations, SC1 and SC2 SNAIL viruses seem to generalize to the striatum and GPe, though they may not be as robust as they are within the cortical context.

claim: Among the 11 SVMs comparing PV+ neuron open-chromatin against PV- cells, EXC neurons, VIP+ neurons, or SST+ neurons, 124 well-supported motifs were recovered.
source: Among the 11 SVMs comparing PV+ neuron open-chromatin against PV- cells, EXC neurons, VIP+ neurons, or SST+ neurons, we recovered 124 well-supported motifs.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: UPGMA clustering on the 124 motifs by sequence similarity identified 14 motif clusters.
source: Thus, we performed UPGMA clustering on the 124 motifs by sequence similarity using STAMP (Mahony and Benos, 2007) and identified 14 motif clusters (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The largest cluster, with 23 motif members, contained representation from all 11 models and had matches to known motifs including the motifs for Esrrg and Rora.
source: The largest cluster, with 23 motif members, contained representation from all 11 models and had matches to known motifs including the motifs for Esrrg and Rora (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: Esrrg transcript levels were differentially overexpressed in the PV+ neuron cluster relative the rest of the frontal cortex in snRNA-seq.
source: Consistent with an important role for Esrrg in PV+ neurons, Esrrg (a.k.a. Err3) transcript levels were differentially overexpressed in the PV+ neuron cluster relative the rest of the frontal cortex in snRNA-seq (DropViz subcluster #2–7 Neuron.Gad1Gad2.Pvalb Esrrg fold ratio = 8.0, p=1.14 × 10–198) (Saunders et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Esrrg and Rora are key TFs in the Pgc1a transcriptional program, which regulates Pvalb expression, mitochondrial function, and transmitter release.
source: Esrrg and Rora are key TFs in the Pgc1a transcriptional program, which regulates Pvalb expression, mitochondrial function, and transmitter release (Lin et al., 2005; Lucas et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Pgc1a signaling is restricted to PV+ neurons in the brain and may mediate the unique energy demands of fast-spiking neurons.
source: Pgc1a signaling is restricted to PV+ neurons in the brain and may mediate the unique energy demands of fast-spiking neurons (Paul et al., 2017; Lucas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The second-largest motif cluster contained 16 motifs, also representing all 11 models, and the motifs had the best matches to motifs for Mef2a, Mef2c, and Mef2d.
source: The second-largest motif cluster contained 16 motifs, also representing all 11 models, and the motifs had the best matches to motifs for Mef2a, Mef2c, and Mef2d.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: A cluster of Lhx6-like motifs was detected with high support from PV+ vs. PV- models and PV+ vs. EXC models.
source: A cluster of Lhx6-like motifs, a TF necessary for MGE interneuron differentiation from interneuron progenitors (Liodis et al., 2007; Vogt et al., 2014), was detected with high support from PV+ vs. PV- models and PV+ vs. EXC models, detected with low support from PV+ vs. VIP+ models, and not detected between MGE neuron subtypes PV+ vs. SST+.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, supported by citations.

claim: Lhx6 is a TF necessary for MGE interneuron differentiation from interneuron progenitors.
source: A cluster of Lhx6-like motifs, a TF necessary for MGE interneuron differentiation from interneuron progenitors (Liodis et al., 2007; Vogt et al., 2014), was detected with high support from PV+ vs. PV- models and PV+ vs. EXC models, detected with low support from PV+ vs. VIP+ models, and not detected between MGE neuron subtypes PV+ vs. SST+.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Two clusters of motifs were dominated by PV+ vs. VIP+ activity, including matches for Stat6, Nkx28, and Cux2 motifs.
source: Interestingly, two clusters of motifs were dominated by PV+ vs. VIP+ activity, including matches for Stat6, Nkx28, and Cux2 motifs.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: Cux2 expression is induced by Lhx6 in the MGE, supporting a role in specification of the MGE interneuron lineage from other interneuron lineages.
source: Cux2 expression is induced by Lhx6 in the MGE, supporting a role in specification of the MGE interneuron lineage (including PV+ and SST+ neurons) from other interneuron lineages (Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: SC1 contained two Esrrg motifs near the sequence center that were high contributors to the PV+ neuron-specific model predictions.
source: SC1 contained two Esrrg motifs near the sequence center that were high contributors to the PV+ neuron-specific model predictions and matched TF-MoDISco motifs for every model (Figure 5b).

claim: SC2 contained a highly important Mef2 sequence near the center.
source: SC2 contained a highly important Mef2 sequence near the center (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: SC2 contained an Esrrg motif with shared importance across all models.
source: Additionally, SC2 contained an Esrrg motif with shared importance across all models.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: The most important features of the SC2 sequence closely resemble those of successful PV+ probe E29 from Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020.
source: Interestingly, the most important features of the SC2 sequence closely resemble those of successful PV+ probe E29 from Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Disruption of Esrrg and Mef2 motifs within SC1 or SC2 resulted in a sharply decreased prediction of PV+ specificity according to the scores across the SVMs.
source: Disruption of Esrrg and Mef2 motifs within SC1 or SC2 resulted in a sharply decreased prediction of PV+ specificity according to the scores across the SVMs (Figure 5d).

claim: Human PV+ SVMs were built using single-nucleus open chromatin data from the human cortex.
source: To investigate this, we built human PV+ SVMs analogous to the mouse SVMs using single-nucleus open chromatin data from the human cortex (Corces et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: Human-trained models were able to reasonably perform the classification task, with auROC 0.73–0.83 and auPRC 0.68–0.81.
source: Although the human data contained fewer cell profiles, models were able to reasonably perform the classification task, with auROC 0.73–0.83 and auPRC 0.68–0.81 (Figure 6a).

claim: Score outputs from human-trained models were correlated with score outputs from mouse-trained models.
source: Score outputs from human-trained models were correlated with score outputs from mouse-trained models (Figure 6b), suggesting shared PV+ neuron-specific enhancer sequence features between mouse and human PV+ neurons.

claim: SC1 was one of the highest-scoring enhancer candidates in both mouse and human SVMs.
source: SC1 was one of the highest-scoring enhancer candidates in both mouse and human SVMs.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis.

claim: The SC1 SNAIL probe was tested in the rhesus macaque cortex via localized intracranial AAV injection.
source: Because SC1 was predicted to retain PV+ neuron specificity in primates, we tested the SC1 SNAIL probe in the rhesus macaque cortex via localized intracranial AAV injection.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: High expression of Sun1GFP with enrichment for PV+ neurons was observed in the rhesus macaque cortex.
source: We observed high expression of Sun1GFP with enrichment for PV+ neurons.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation.

claim: There was a trade-off between precision and recall of PV+ neuron labeling related to the spatial viral load, with a mean precision of 22% near the injection site center and 67% at the periphery.
source: There was a trade-off between precision and recall of PV+ neuron labeling related to the spatial viral load, with a mean precision of 22% near the injection site center and 67% at the periphery.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental validation.

claim: At the injection center, at least 98% of PV+ neurons were transduced by the SC1 SNAIL probe.
source: At the injection center, at least 98% of PV+ neurons were transduced by the SC1 SNAIL probe, while at the periphery, at least 75% of PV+ neurons were transduced.

claim: At the periphery of the injection site, at least 75% of PV+ neurons were transduced by the SC1 SNAIL probe.

claim: Success in cell type-specific AAV creation has been limited to intensive screens of dozens of individual AAV enhancer candidates in which most do not produce highly selective expression.
source: Thus far, success in cell type-specific AAV creation has been limited to intensive screens of dozens of individual AAV enhancer candidates in which most do not produce highly selective expression (Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020; Mich et al., 2021; Graybuck et al., 2021).

claim: Machine learning classifiers are incorporated as an additional filter for improved enhancer pre-selection in order to mitigate the experimental burden.
source: In SNAIL, our framework for cell type-specific AAV engineering, we incorporate machine learning classifiers as an additional filter for improved enhancer pre-selection in order to mitigate the experimental burden.
evidence: This describes the approach of the study.

claim: On a set of externally tested PV+ enhancer-driven AAVs, the average PV+ specificity score across classifiers was more predictive of PV+ specific AAV expression than the log2 fold difference of snATAC-seq signal, sequence conservation, or accessibility conservation at these loci.
source: On a set of externally tested PV+ enhancer-driven AAVs (Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020), the average PV+ specificity score across our classifiers was more predictive of PV+ specific AAV expression than the log2 fold difference of snATAC-seq signal, sequence conservation, or accessibility conservation at these loci.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: The incorporation of differential sequence property analyses will continue to improve the throughput of targeted AAV development in new contexts.
source: We believe that the incorporation of differential sequence property analyses will continue to improve the throughput of targeted AAV development in new contexts and make cell type-specific enhancer tool development accessible for more researchers.

source: In the cortex, Esrrg expression is mainly restricted to PV+ neurons and Lhx6 is restricted to MGE interneurons, but Mef2 transcripts are widely expressed in many inhibitory and excitatory neurons.
